issues.body: `crate_is_still_unpublished` only checks that a declaration line starts with `publish` and contains the substring `false`. Cargo also accepts a registry allow-list for `package.publish`; for example `publish = ["false"]` is publishable to the registry named `false`, yet this test passes. Thus removing the real `publish = false` premise need not fire trigger (b), contradicting the README and deferral record.
issues.fix_hint: Parse the package manifest as TOML/Cargo metadata and assert that `package.publish` is the boolean `false`. If avoiding a parser is required, at minimum parse the assignment and require the trimmed RHS to equal exactly `false`, with a regression test covering a registry list containing the word `false`.
issues.title: Publication trip-wire accepts publishable manifests

issues.body: `nothing_in_the_workspace_depends_on_sparq_gpu` searches only each `crates/*/Cargo.toml` for the literal string `sparq-gpu`. A root `[workspace.dependencies] gpu = { package = "sparq-gpu", ... }` plus `gpu.workspace = true` in a member is a valid Cargo dependency, but the member manifest contains no `sparq-gpu` string and the root manifest is never scanned. The test therefore stays green after integration, invalidating exit trigger (a).
issues.fix_hint: Use resolved Cargo metadata and inspect dependency package identities for every workspace member other than `sparq-gpu`, rather than grepping manifest text. Add a fixture or focused parser-level regression test for a renamed, workspace-inherited dependency.
issues.title: Dependency trip-wire misses inherited workspace dependencies

verdict.summary: The deferral record is careful about scope and candid about unresolved GPU risks, but both load-bearing trip-wires use textual heuristics that do not actually enforce the conditions the documentation claims. Valid Cargo manifest forms can make the crate publishable or introduce a workspace dependency while these tests remain green. Because the safety rationale rests on those conditions being mechanically self-firing, these are major correctness gaps rather than robustness nits.
